title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 41 — Global depository receipt

content.overview: A company may issue depository receipts in a foreign country only after a special resolution in general meeting and in the prescribed manner, subject to prescribed conditions.
content.glance: A company may issue depository receipts in a foreign country only after a special resolution in general meeting and in the prescribed manner, subject to prescribed conditions.
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 41 (Global depository receipts). A company may issue depository receipts in a foreign country only after passing a special resolution in its general meeting and in the prescribed manner, subject to prescribed conditions. Section 41 supplies the corporate-approval gateway; the issue must also comply with applicable rules and any relevant securities, foreign-exchange, depository or listing requirements. It is not a standalone permission to disregard those regimes. Distinguish this route from section 40 public-offer requirements and section 42 private placement.

sections.heading: Corporate approval
sections.body: The company must pass a special resolution in general meeting before issuing depository receipts under section 41.

sections.heading: Foreign issue and prescribed conditions
sections.body: The depository receipts are issued in a foreign country and the issue must follow the prescribed manner and conditions.

sections.heading: Other regulatory requirements
sections.body: Applicable securities, foreign-exchange, depository, listing and prescribed rules may operate alongside section 41. Verify the current framework for the particular issue.

sections.heading: Distinction from connected provisions
sections.body: Section 40 addresses public offers and related requirements; section 42 governs private placement. Neither substitutes for the section 41 special-resolution route where it applies.

examples.title: Illustration 1
examples.body: A company proposes a foreign depository-receipt issue without first obtaining the required special resolution. The section 41 authorisation condition has not been satisfied.

examples.title: Illustration 2
examples.body: A special resolution has been passed, but the company ignores a mandatory prescribed condition governing the issue. The resolution alone does not establish full compliance.

examples.title: Illustration 3
examples.body: A company analyses section 41 together with the applicable prescribed framework rather than treating the bare section as the entire transaction code.

hypotheticals.question: A company approves a foreign depository-receipt issue only by Board resolution. Is that enough?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 41 expressly requires a special resolution in general meeting, followed by compliance with the prescribed manner and conditions.

hypotheticals.question: Does section 41 alone establish compliance for a cross-border receipt issue?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Apply the prescribed conditions and any relevant securities, foreign-exchange, depository or listing requirements.

distinctions.title: Global depository receipts and other issue routes
distinctions.left: Section 41 governs foreign depository receipts with a special-resolution requirement.
distinctions.right: Section 40 governs public-offer/exchange requirements; section 42 governs private placement.

misconceptions.trap: Treating an ordinary Board resolution as sufficient.
misconceptions.correction: Section 41 requires a special resolution in general meeting.

misconceptions.trap: Treating section 41 as an exhaustive code for every international receipt issue.
misconceptions.correction: Apply the prescribed conditions and other relevant regulatory regimes.

misconceptions.trap: Using section 42 private placement or section 40 public-offer rules as a substitute for section 41 authorisation.
misconceptions.correction: Identify and apply each relevant statutory route separately.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What is the express corporate approval under section 41?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: A special resolution in general meeting.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What else must be checked?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: The prescribed manner and conditions and any relevant securities, foreign-exchange, depository or listing requirements.
